title: Noise on Real Devices
summary: T1 relaxation, T2 dephasing, readout and gate errors, and how an idle qubit loses population and coherence.
objectives: Convert T1, T2 and an idle time into the parameters of amplitude damping and phase damping
Simulate an idling qubit with a density matrix and read its population and coherence
Check that population decays as exp(−t/T1) and coherence as exp(−t/T2)
mission: A qubit in |+⟩ idles for t_wait with relaxation time T1 and coherence time T2. In the QNode idle(T1, T2, t_wait), apply amplitude damping followed by phase damping so that the population of |1⟩ decays as exp(−t/T1) and the coherence as exp(−t/T2). Then store in p1 the probability of measuring 1 and in coherence the size |ρ01| of the off-diagonal element.

prediction.question: A qubit has T1 = 50 µs. Which coherence time T2 is impossible?
prediction.explanation: Relaxation alone dephases the qubit: amplitude damping already shrinks the coherence as exp(−t/(2·T1)). Any other process can only shorten T2, so T2 ≤ 2·T1 = 100 µs. T2 = 100 µs is the limit with no pure dephasing, and 120 µs would need negative dephasing.

hints: Amplitude damping with parameter γ takes ρ11 to (1 − γ)·ρ11. For the population to decay as exp(−t/T1), take γ = 1 − exp(−t_wait/T1) and apply qml.AmplitudeDamping(gamma, wires=0).

Amplitude damping also multiplies the coherence by √(1 − γ) = exp(−t/(2·T1)). The target is exp(−t/T2), so the missing decay comes from pure dephasing with rate 1/T_phi = 1/T2 − 1/(2·T1). Phase damping with parameter λ multiplies the coherence by √(1 − λ), so λ = 1 − exp(−2·t_wait/T_phi).

Apply qml.AmplitudeDamping(gamma, wires=0) and qml.PhaseDamping(lam, wires=0) after the Hadamard gate. Then rho = idle(T1, T2, t_wait), p1 = np.real(rho[1, 1]) and coherence = np.abs(rho[0, 1]). Expect p1 = exp(−t/T1)/2 and coherence = exp(−t/T2)/2.
